q: How much does a roof replacement cost in Knoxville?
a: Most asphalt shingle replacements on Knoxville-area homes of about 2,000 square feet land around $15,000 to $30,000. Size and pitch, a second layer to tear off, rotted decking and the shingle line you pick all move the number. Your free inspection gets you a written estimate, so you can see where the money goes. For a planning range on your own house, try the roof cost calculator.

q: Why do roofing quotes vary so much?
a: Because they often aren't pricing the same roof. One quote includes full tear-off, ice-and-water membrane in the valleys, and fresh pipe boots and flashing. Another reuses the flashing, skips the membrane and bills rotted decking later. Ask each roofer for an estimate and compare the scope.

q: Do you offer financing?
a: We provide a written estimate you can take to your bank or credit union. See our payment options for questions to ask when comparing loans.

q: Will the price change once you start?
a: Your written proposal explains what's included and how concealed damage will be priced. If removing the existing roof reveals work outside that scope, we'll show you the problem and get your approval before proceeding.

q: Is a metal roof more expensive than shingles?
a: Up front, usually yes. Metal costs noticeably more to install than architectural shingles, and standing seam costs more than exposed-fastener panels. In return you get a longer life and less upkeep, which matters on steep cabin roofs and for owners who plan to stay. Ask for both prices at your free inspection and compare them on paper.

q: Is the inspection really free?
a: Yes. There's no charge and nothing to sign. We check the shingles, the flashing, the pipe boots and valleys, and the gutters and roof edge, then tell you what we found in plain English. If the roof needs work, you get a written estimate. If it's fine, we'll say so.

q: Do I need to be home for the inspection?
a: Not for the outside check, as long as we can get into the yard. If you'd like the attic checked for water stains, daylight or poor airflow, someone has to let us in. If you can't be there, you'll still hear what we found, plus a written estimate if the roof needs work.

q: Can I just text you a photo?
a: Please do. Text a photo of the problem (the ceiling stain, the shingles on the ground, the spot you can see from the street) to (865) 567-0233 with your address. We'll text back what it looks like and whether someone needs to come out. It's the fastest way to find out if a problem is small.

q: What's the satellite view on your website for?
a: It shows your own roof from above, so you can point to the spot you're worried about when you call. Satellite photos can be years old and too blurry to show damage, so they don't replace an inspection. Your address goes to Google to draw the map; we only get it if you send the form.

q: After a storm, should I call my insurance company or a roofer first?
a: Start with an inspection so you know what damage is there and what repairs may cost. If you file a claim, we provide photos and an itemized construction estimate, and meet your adjuster to explain the work. Your insurer decides coverage.

q: Will my insurance pay for a replacement roof?
a: Your insurer decides based on your policy and the cause of the damage. Hail and wind damage may be covered; wear and age are generally treated differently. We document the roof's condition and provide a repair estimate for the adjuster's review.

q: Who pays the deductible?
a: You do. Your deductible is your share of the claim, and we never waive it, cover it, or rebate it. A roofer who offers to "take care of your deductible" is putting your claim at risk, so walk away. Some policies carry a separate wind or hail deductible. Check your declarations page so the number isn't a surprise.

q: Do you work with my insurance company?
a: We provide damage photos and an itemized repair estimate, and meet your adjuster to explain the construction scope. We can also document hidden damage found during tear-off. Your insurer determines coverage and payment.

q: What if my claim is denied or only partly paid?
a: Ask your insurance company to put the reasons in writing. Then we compare them to our photos. If something was missed, we re-inspect, photograph the specific areas and send your adjuster an itemized estimate for them. Sometimes the decision holds up, and a repair is the right next step.

q: Can I cancel a roofing contract if my claim is denied?
a: Yes. Under Tennessee law, if your roofing contract depends on an insurance claim and your insurer says in writing that the damage isn't covered, you can cancel by midnight of the third business day after that notice (T.C.A. § 62-6-602 and § 62-6-603). Money you paid, except for emergency repairs already done, comes back within 10 business days.

q: How long does a roof replacement take?
a: One to three days for a typical house once the materials arrive. Size, pitch, decking and the weather all change that, and rain can push the start date. You'll have the schedule in writing before work begins, and anything opened up gets closed or tarped before the crew leaves each night.

q: What happens if you find rotted wood under the shingles?
a: It gets replaced, and only the boards that are actually soft. Rotted decking won't hold nails, and shingles over soft wood fail early. Your written estimate already lists the cost per sheet, so you know the number before work starts.

q: Do you tear off the old roof or go over it?
a: We remove the old roofing so we can check the decking and replace damaged wood. Adding another layer can hide problems and add weight. Your proposal states the tear-off scope.

q: What about my yard, flower beds and nails in the driveway?
a: Tarps go over the flower beds and anything close to the house, debris goes straight into the dumpster, and a magnet sweep runs over the yard and driveway at the end. When the job is done, the dumpster goes too. If you find a nail later, call us and we'll come back for it.

q: Do you pull the permit?
a: We check the requirements for your property and handle any permits your project needs.

q: What shingles do you install?
a: Mostly architectural shingles, which are thicker than the old flat 3-tab kind and hold up better in wind, with ridge caps from the same line so the colors match. We install lines from the major makers, including impact-resistant shingles for hail and algae-resistant ones for shady slopes. If you'd rather have metal, we price that too.

q: Can you fix a leak instead of replacing the whole roof?
a: Usually, yes. Most leaks start at a handful of spots: cracked pipe boots, flashing at a wall or chimney, a few wind-lifted shingles, or a skylight. Each can usually be fixed on its own, and if a repair will stop the leak, that's what we quote. We'll also tell you when patching has become throwing money away.

q: My roof is leaking right now. What do I do?
a: Put a bucket under the drip and move anything valuable. Keep people away from a bulging or sagging ceiling. Take photos, and stay off the roof in the rain. Then call or text (865) 567-0233. Emergency calls are answered around the clock.

q: Will my HOA have a say in my roof?
a: In a lot of Knoxville-area subdivisions, yes. Many covenants set rules on shingle color and sometimes material, and the HOA wants its review form signed off before work starts. We'll fill in the manufacturer, line and color for the form, and material gets ordered only after the HOA says yes in writing.

q: Why are there black streaks on my roof?
a: That's almost always algae. Knoxville gets about 52 inches of rain a year and stays humid all summer, and algae grows on shady, north-facing slopes. It's mostly cosmetic. Pressure washing strips granules and shortens the roof's life, so don't. When you replace, an algae-resistant shingle keeps it away longer.

q: Do you work on cabins and rental properties?
a: Yes. Cabins and rental homes are welcome, and they often have steep pitches and metal roofs, both of which we work on. A property manager can book an inspection for a place they don't live at; just give us the address and how to reach the yard. If you look after more than one property, each gets its own written estimate.

q: What if replacement shingles don't match the rest of my roof?
a: It happens a lot, because colors get discontinued and old shingles fade. For a repair, we find the closest match we can, and you can see a sample before it goes on. After a storm claim, ask your insurer in writing how your policy treats a roof that won't match.

q: Do I need gutter guards?
a: Guards may help where leaves and pine needles repeatedly clog the gutters, but they still need maintenance. On an open roof with little debris, they may add little value. We check the tree cover and drainage, then price the gutters with and without guards.

q: Who will I actually deal with?
a: Call or text (865) 567-0233 with questions. You'll have a named contact while the job is underway and an estimate before work begins.

q: Do you do commercial roofing?
a: Yes. We work on low-slope roofs over stores, offices, warehouses and church halls, with TPO and EPDM membranes, coatings and metal. Flat roofs usually leak at seams, drains, wall flashing and anything that pokes through, so that's where we look first. Property managers get a written scope and price they can put in front of an owner.

q: Which areas do you cover?
a: All of East Tennessee. We work across Knox, Blount, Loudon, Anderson, Roane, Sevier, Jefferson, Hamblen, Grainger, Union, Monroe and Cocke counties, from Knoxville and Farragut out to Maryville, Sevierville, Oak Ridge, Lenoir City and Morristown. Not sure we reach you? Text your address to (865) 567-0233 and you'll get a straight answer.

q: My ceiling is stained near the chimney. Is it the chimney or the roof?
a: Usually it's the joint between them. Flashing runs under the shingles where the chimney comes through, and counterflashing set into the brick laps over it. When either pulls loose or rusts, rain runs down into your ceiling. We fix flashing, add crickets and seal crowns. If the brick itself is crumbling, you need a mason, and we'll say so.

q: My skylight leaks. Can it be fixed, or does it need replacing?
a: Most skylight leaks come from the flashing around the frame, not the glass. If the unit is sound, we reseal or reflash it, lifting the shingles around it and putting in fresh flashing. If the glass has fogged between the panes or the frame is cracked, replacing the unit makes more sense. Text us a photo to start.

q: Do you install siding?
a: Yes: vinyl, fiber cement and engineered wood. Vinyl is the most common around Knoxville and the cheapest to keep up. Fiber cement is heavier and holds paint well. Engineered wood looks like real lap siding at less weight. We check the flashing and roof drainage as part of the plan, so the new siding helps protect the wall behind it.

q: Do you replace windows and doors?
a: Yes, replacement windows and entry doors, and they can go in alongside siding so the trim and flashing get done once. For energy ratings, read the sticker. The U-factor shows how well a window holds heat in over winter, and lower is better. The solar heat gain number shows how much summer sun gets through as heat.

q: Can you work around our church's services and events?
a: Yes. Tell us what's on the calendar (Sunday services, weddings, funerals, Vacation Bible School) and the loud work gets planned around it. Many churches have a steep sanctuary roof and a flat fellowship hall roof, and we price both. A building committee gets a written scope with each part of the job and its cost.

q: Can I pay for my roof over time?
a: You can take our written estimate to your own bank or credit union to discuss payment options. Compare the total repayment cost, fees, rate changes and early-payoff terms before choosing a loan.

q: Do I have to use my insurer's roofer?
a: No. Your insurer may send you a list of roofers it works with, and you can call one of them if you like. You can also hire your own. The roofer you hire works for you, not for the insurance company. Pick the one whose written estimate and straight answers you trust.

q: What is a supplement?
a: When the old roof comes off, it sometimes shows damage nobody could see from the top: soft decking, rusted flashing, a second layer of shingles. A supplement is the request that goes back to your insurer for that work. We write it and send it to your insurance company with additional photos and an itemized estimate for what the first estimate missed.

q: How long does a roof insurance claim take?
a: It depends on your insurer and how hard the storm hit. After a big hailstorm, adjusters and roofers are booked up for weeks. The parts you control: get the inspection early, file promptly, and keep the photos and the estimate together. Most of the waiting sits between filing and the adjuster's visit, and between the adjuster's report and the first check.

q: Do you build decks?
a: Yes. We build decks, front and back porches, screened porches and covered patios around Knoxville. Where a cover ties into the house, a roofer is the right builder: the porch roof gets flashed into the main roof and shingled to match. The frame is pressure-treated lumber, and the boards are composite or wood, your choice. Book a free visit to discuss the design and get a written estimate.

q: Does a deck need a permit?
a: We check the requirements for your property and handle any permits your project needs. Your HOA may also need to approve the design.

q: Can you repair just one spot on my roof?
a: Yes, and most of the time that's the right call. A cracked pipe boot, a few missing shingles or a loose piece of flashing can be fixed on its own. The hard part is matching: shingle colors get discontinued and old ones fade, so ask to see a sample before it goes on. If the roof is worn out across whole slopes, a single repair buys little time, and we'll tell you so.

q: Is it a repair or a replacement?
a: Look at the whole roof, not just the leak. If the shingles lie flat, still have their granules and the roof has good years left, fix the spot. If leaks keep showing up in other places, shingles are curling or cracking across whole slopes, or the roof is 20 years old or more, replacement is usually the better money. When it's close, ask for both prices in writing and compare.

q: What should I do first after a storm hits my roof?
a: Get everyone out of any room where the ceiling took a hit, and look for downed power lines from a window before you go outside. Put buckets under the drips and move what can't get wet. Take photos and video of the damage from a few angles before anything gets moved, and stay off the roof. If a tree is on the house, the tree crew goes first. Then call or text (865) 567-0233 to get a tarp on.

q: Does a Knoxville roof replacement need a permit?
a: We check the requirements for your property and handle any permits your project needs. A Knoxville mailing address alone doesn't establish which office covers the property.

q: What are your hours?
a: The office is open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and 24-hour emergency service is available if water is coming in. For anything else, call or text (865) 567-0233 during the week, text us a photo of the problem, or fill in the form on any page and we'll call you back to set a time.

q: What happens during a free roof inspection?
a: We check the roof covering, flashing, vents, valleys, gutters and edges. On a house, accessible attic areas can help us trace water stains or ventilation problems. You'll hear what we found, whether it needs attention and what we recommend next.

q: Should I repair or replace my roof?
a: If the trouble is one spot on a roof that's otherwise sound, with shingles lying flat, granules still on and good years left, a repair is the right call. If the damage covers several slopes, the shingles are curling or bald, or leaks keep turning up in different places, it's usually time to replace. After your free inspection you can have both prices in writing and compare them side by side.

q: Why choose Crestone?
a: Ryan Dix leads Crestone Roofing in Knoxville. You can call or text the team, ask questions about the work and review the scope before deciding. See our projects for examples of the Crestone family's roofing work.

q: What usually voids a roof warranty?
a: A few things come up again and again: repairs made later with parts that don't match the original system, an attic that can't breathe, satellite dishes or other mounts screwed through the shingles, pressure washing that strips the granules, and heavy foot traffic from other trades. The shingle maker's own terms are the ones that count, so read them. Our warranty page covers what to get in writing.

q: Can you inspect my roof the same day?
a: Call or text us Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and we inspect your roof the same day. Reach us after hours or on a weekend and we come out the next weekday morning.
